input.plan:
# `intropy deploy init` — scaffold GitOps manifests from the topology

## Context

Onboarding a component into the GitOps repo is entirely manual today. `internal/gitops/layout.go`'s
`notFoundError` literally instructs the user to hand-create
`domains/<domain>/<system>/<component>/{component.yaml,base,overlays}`. Everything downstream is
automated — `intropy deploy` pins digests, `promote` copies them, `status`/`diff`/`sync` read ArgoCD — but
the tree itself is typed out by hand, per component, per environment, per customer.

`intropy manifests create` was an earlier attempt (added `f9fc2229`, removed `90dd4838` on 2026-07-26) and
failed for two recorded reasons: it rendered into `./deploy` **inside the component repo**, which nothing
consumes because ArgoCD reads the GitOps repo; and it pinned `newTag: latest`, contradicting the
digest-pinning discipline `deploy` exists to enforce. This design corrects both.

Outcome: after `intropy deploy init`, every file ArgoCD needs exists and every fact the CLI can derive is
filled in. What's left is a bounded, greppable list of placeholders — connection strings, hosts,
credentials, cron schedules — that only a human can supply. Complete manifests are explicitly a non-goal.

## What the existing customer repos already establish

Read from `~/dev/intropy/customers/*/gitops` — the design follows these rather than inventing conventions.

- **`scopes:` is already the convention** on every Dapr `Component`, listing the app-ids permitted to use it.
- **Dapr components belong in `base/`, identical across environments.** fluxia puts them per-overlay and
  varies the broker (`pubsub.in-memory` in dev, `pubsub.rabbitmq` in prod); that is a **deviation we are not
  following**. One broker type per system, one file, all environments. What legitimately differs per
  environment is the *credential*, not the component — and a Dapr `Component` references its secret by
  name (`secretKeyRef`), so identical YAML in `base/` resolves to different values in each environment's
  namespace. Overlays stay thin: `namespace`, `resources: [../../base]`, and the image pin `deploy` writes.
- **Extractors are `CronJob`s**, not Deployments — confirmed in both `fluxia/gitops/.../order-extractor`
  and `entrovia/gitops/.../order-extractor` and `entrovia/.../relex-fno`. Other blocks are Deployments.
- **The namespace is set by the overlay and not created by the customer repo.** fluxia uses a flat
  `namespace: integrations`; per my notes entrovia uses `{test,prod}-<slug>-integrations`, provisioned by
  `~/dev/intropy/platform/service-plane/gitops` along with Dapr itself, RabbitMQ, Vault and the
  `harbor-intropy-robot-credentials` / `rabbitmq-connection` secrets. **Customer repos must not install
  those.** So namespace is a parameter and `Namespace` objects are never emitted.
- **Image repositories differ per customer**: `harbor.intropy.io/fluxia/order-extractor` vs
  `harbor.intropy.io/integrations/int123`. The repo pattern is a parameter, not `<registry>/integrations/<name>`.
- **`system-host` is the only template with no Dockerfile** (extractor, loader, transactional and
  hello-world all have one). The host is a composition root, not a deployed container — it has no image.

### A live bug this surfaced, worth fixing separately

Two of fluxia's Applications both own `Component/pubsub` in namespace `integrations`:

| file | name | type | scopes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `order-management/INT123/overlays/dev/pubsub.yaml` | `pubsub` | `pubsub.in-memory` | `int123` |
| `orders/order-flow/order-extractor/overlays/dev/pubsub.yaml` | `pubsub` | `pubsub.in-memory` | `order-extractor`, `order-loader` |

Same name, same namespace, different specs, two ArgoCD Applications — last sync wins and the other reports
drift. Note also that the extractor's overlay owns a Component scoped to its *sibling* `order-loader`
(the arbitrary-owner pattern), and that `order-extractor/overlays/prod/pubsub.yaml` is `pubsub.in-memory`
scoped to two app-ids, which cannot work across pods and looks like a copy-paste bug. Not in scope here,
but `deploy init`'s single-owner rule is what prevents it recurring.

## Decisions taken

| | |
|---|---|
| **Provider** | Repo-level `platform: {provider, pubsub, secretStore}` in `deploy.yaml`. One platform per repo, uniform across environments — no per-environment override. |
| **Write mode** | Create `deploy-init/<domain>-<system>`, commit only the staged paths, push the branch, restore the default branch. Never pushes to the default branch — a placeholder-bearing tree would be picked up by the ApplicationSet immediately. |
| **Scope** | Per-block tree **plus** a system-level directory for the system host, which owns the shared Dapr objects. |
| **Shared objects' owner** | The **system host** gets its own component directory. Exactly one Application owns each Dapr `Component`; `scopes:` lists the app-ids allowed to use it. |
| **Image-less directories** | New `kind: service` (default) / `kind: shared` on `component.yaml`; images required only for `service`. |
| **Conditionality** | `spec.files[]` with `when` in `template.yaml`. First match decides; an unmatched path is included, so every existing template renders byte-identically to today. |

### Why the host owns the shared objects

A Dapr `Component` is namespace-scoped, and all of a customer's integrations share one namespace. So
`metadata.name: pubsub` is a single Kubernetes object for the whole namespace and exactly one ArgoCD
Application may own it. `scopes:` controls which app-ids may *use* the component; it does not change the
name, so it does not prevent the collision — it is the right complement to single ownership, not a
substitute for it (fluxia's table above is what "scopes without single ownership" looks like).

Putting them in the host directory rather than an invented `shared/` means the gitops tree mirrors the
code layout and reuses a name that already exists in the topology and in `.intropy/scaffold.json`
(`RoleSystemHost`). The host has no Dockerfile and therefore no image, which is exactly what `kind: shared`
describes.

Kustomize *would* let each block reference the host directory via `resources: [../../../host/base]` — the
repo already relies on upward traversal for `../../base`. It is the wrong tool here: N blocks referencing
it means N Applications rendering and claiming the same object, and
`internal/kustomize/manifest.go` builds each overlay and diffs the rendered stream, so the shared objects
would appear inside every block's `deploy diff`. No reference is needed anyway — a Dapr `Component` is not
a kustomize dependency of a Deployment; the sidecar resolves it by name through the Dapr control plane at
runtime. Ordering, if it ever matters, is an ArgoCD sync-wave annotation on the host directory.

## Target tree

```
domains/sales/ordersync/
  host/                                 kind: shared — no image, nothing to pin
    component.yaml
    base/
      kustomization.yaml
      dapr/pubsub.yaml                  in-memory | rabbitmq | servicebus — one per repo platform
      dapr/secretstore.yaml
      dapr/binding-<connector>.yaml     one per topology connector, when connectors exist
      secrets/secrets.yaml              REPLACE-ME-* stubs, referenced by secretKeyRef
    overlays/dev/kustomization.yaml     namespace: <parameter>, resources: [../../base]
    overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml    identical but for the namespace
    README.md                            what each placeholder is and where to get it
  order-extract/                        kind: service — extractor ⇒ CronJob
    component.yaml
    base/{cronjob.yaml,kustomization.yaml}
    overlays/{dev,prod}/kustomization.yaml
  order-load/                           kind: service — loader ⇒ Deployment
    component.yaml
    base/{deployment.yaml,kustomization.yaml}
    overlays/{dev,prod}/kustomization.yaml
```

No `Namespace` object anywhere — the service-plane provisions it. Images are left at the `:unpinned`
sentinel; `intropy deploy` is the only thing that pins. Because the environment comes from the
ApplicationSet's cluster generator rather than the path (see step 3), the host directory needs an overlay
for **every** environment in `deploy.yaml`, not a subset.

## Work breakdown

Steps 1–4 are independent. Step 11 is a cross-repo prereq that can proceed in parallel from the start.

### 1. Conditional file filter in `internal/template`

`internal/template/manifest.go` — add to `Spec`:

```go
// FileRule conditionally includes part of a skeleton. Path is a slash-separated
// glob relative to skeleton/, matched against the *source* path with any .tmpl
// suffix included; a trailing "/**" also matches everything beneath the
// directory. When is a Go template (sprig available) rendered against the
// resolved values; any result other than "", "false" or "0" includes the match.
// The first rule whose Path matches decides, and a path no rule matches is
// included — so a template without spec.files renders exactly as before.
type FileRule struct {
    Path string `yaml:"path" json:"path"`
    When string `yaml:"when" json:"when"`
}
```

Three obligations that are easy to miss:

- `Files` must also be added to the **shadow `rawSpec` struct inside `Spec.UnmarshalYAML`**
  (`manifest.go:66`) — it decodes into `rawSpec`, so a field added only to `Spec` is silently dropped.
- `validate()` rejects an empty `path`, rejects an empty `when` (a rule with no condition is an authoring
  error), and **pre-parses each `when`** so a syntax error surfaces at `LoadTemplate`, not mid-render.
- Matching is against the **source** path, not the rendered one: a rule that decides on values cannot
  depend on a path values produce. Document that a `{{ .name }}/` segment is only reachable via a glob.

New `internal/template/filter.go`:

```go
type skeletonFilter struct {
    rules  []FileRule
    values map[string]any
    cache  map[int]bool // a when depends only on values — evaluate each rule once
}
func newSkeletonFilter(rules []FileRule, values map[string]any) *skeletonFilter
func (f *skeletonFilter) include(rel string) (bool, error)
func matchSkeletonPath(pattern, rel string) bool
func truthy(rendered string) bool
```

`include` evaluates `when` with the **existing `renderExpr` (`internal/template/values.go:220`)** — no new
expression language. `renderExpr` sets `Option("missingkey=error")`, so a typo'd value name is a loud
error rather than a silent skip. Booleans are real booleans by then (`coerceKnownFieldValue`), so
`{{ .externalSecrets }}` renders `true`/`false`.

`internal/template/render.go` — extract the walk:

```go
func RenderFiltered(srcDir, destDir string, values map[string]any, rules []FileRule) error
func Render(srcDir, destDir string, values map[string]any) error {
    return RenderFiltered(srcDir, destDir, values, nil)
}
```

In the existing `WalkDir` callback, right after `rel` is computed and **before** `renderPath`:

```go
rel = filepath.ToSlash(rel)
include, err := filter.include(rel)
if err != nil { return err }
if !include {
    if d.IsDir() { return fs.SkipDir }
    return nil
}
```

`int create` and the dependency path keep calling `Render` and are provably unaffected.

**Tests** (`internal/template/filter_test.go` plus additions to `render_test.go`) — string constants and
`t.TempDir()`, per `CONTRIBUTING.md`:

- No rules → everything rendered. The regression guard for `int create`.
- `when` true → present; false → absent.
- `dapr/**` false → whole subtree absent, **and a file inside it with a deliberately malformed template
  body does not fail the render**. This proves pruning happens before parsing; an implementation that
  filters after walking fails it.
- First-match-wins with two overlapping rules.
- `when` referencing an undefined value → error.
- Truthiness table: `""`/`"false"`/`"0"` excluded; `"true"`/`"1"`/`"yes"` included.
- `LoadTemplate` rejects empty `path`, empty `when`, malformed `{{`.
- `Spec.UnmarshalYAML` preserves `files` — the shadow-struct trap.

### 2. `InjectReserved` in `internal/template`

Param types are scalar-only (`fieldFromSchema`, `manifest.go:150`); widening them would ripple through
`coerce`, `Fields`, `AutoPrompter`, `applySetValues`, `--set` syntax and the dashboard form code. **Do not
widen them.** Promote the deleted command's one good idea — reserved keys injected *after* schema
validation — into a shared helper:

```go
// internal/template/values.go
const (
    ReservedTopologyKey  = "topology"
    ReservedComponentKey = "component"
    ReservedGitopsKey    = "gitops"
    ReservedScaffoldKey  = "scaffold"
)

// InjectReserved adds structured, non-parameter data to a resolved value map
// after JSON Schema validation, so a skeleton can range over data that is not
// expressible as a scalar parameter. It refuses any key that collides with a
// declared parameter or a spec.values entry.
func InjectReserved(t *Template, values map[string]any, reserved map[string]any) error
```

1. `--topology <file>` / `-` → `topology.Decode`. **Both the test seam and the CI path**

2. Discover hosts via `template.ListScaffolds(--source-dir)` filtered to `RoleSystemHost`, then `runGraph`.

### 6. The deployment model — `internal/deploy/initmodel.go`

```go

// "topology" key: derived, flattened and sorted. Raw topology.Topology is
// unsuitable — its APIs/Provides/Consumes are json.RawMessage, and neither map
// iteration nor host emission order is stable, which idempotent rendering requires.
type InitModel struct {
    System     string          `json:"system"`
    Host       InitHost        `json:"host"`       // name, appIds it must scope
    Components []InitComponent `json:"components"` // name, kind, appId, workload, topics, connectors
    PubSubs    []InitPubSub    `json:"pubsubs"`    // name + the sorted app-ids to put in scopes:
    Topics     []InitTopic     `json:"topics"`
    Connectors []InitConnector `json:"connectors"` // name, externalSystem, transport, directions, appIds
}
func newInitModel(t *topology.Topology, scaffolds []template.ScaffoldEntry) InitModel
```

`InitComponent.Workload` is `"cronjob"` for `kind == extractor` and `"deployment"` otherwise, matching what
fluxia and entrovia already do. That drives the base file swap via `when`, and it is the single most
valuable thing the topology contributes.

`InitPubSub.AppIDs` is the union of a topic's `Publishers` and `Subscribers` mapped to app-ids — this is
what populates `scopes:`, so the emitted Component grants exactly the blocks the topology says use it.
`InitConnector.AppIDs` does the same from `Connector.UsedBy`.

Sorting everything is load-bearing: idempotency depends on byte-identical re-renders, and neither Go map
order nor host emission order is guaranteed. Inject via a JSON round-trip into `map[string]any` so `index`
and sprig behave uniformly.

Tests from a string-constant topology JSON: extractor → cronjob and loader → deployment; pubsub app-ids
are the sorted union of publishers and subscribers; connectors deduped and sorted; `appId` falls back to
`name`; an unwired component survives.

Never `Render` straight into the tree: `writeAtomically` overwrites, and an overlay contains digests
`deploy` pinned. Render to a fresh staging temp dir, then classify per file.

```go
type fileAction struct {
    Rel    string // repo-relative, slash-separated
    Action string // "create" | "identical" | "skip-exists" | "overwrite"
}
func classifyStaged(stagingDir, destRoot string, force bool) ([]fileAction, error)
func applyStaged(stagingDir, destRoot string, actions []fileAction) error
```

- Fresh onboarding → all `create`.
- Byte-identical existing file → `identical`; not written, not reported as a change.
- Differing existing file → `skip-exists` (reported, not written) unless `--force` → `overwrite`.
- Topology grew a component → only that subtree is `create`; existing components untouched.
  **Additive by default** is what makes this safe to re-run for the system's whole life.
- `--force` **guard**: refuse outright, naming the files, if any target `overlays/<env>/kustomization.yaml`
  carries an `images:` entry with a digest — overwriting that un-deploys production. Read it with the
  existing `kustomize.ReadKustomization`.
- `--plan` prints the actions and returns before `applyStaged`.

`template.EnsureOutputDir` is bypassed — its "refuse a non-empty directory" policy is wrong here;
`classifyStaged` owns the policy.

Tests over a `gitops/gitopstest.NewRepo` fixture: each classification; `--force` refused on a pinned
digest; nothing written if any classification errors.

position), legal inside a URL, self-describing so a grep hit tells you what to supply, one regex to match.

```go

var placeholderPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`REPLACE-ME-[A-Z0-9-]*[A-Z0-9]`)

type Placeholder struct {
    File  string `json:"file"` // repo-relative, slash-separated
    Line  int    `json:"line"`
    Token string `json:"token"`
}
func scanPlaceholders(root string, rels []string) ([]Placeholder, error)
```

writes `.WithSchedule("* * * * *")` into the generated C# but v1 of the record carries nothing, so the CLI
cannot know it and must not guess.

**The unpinned image tag is a different thing and must not be conflated.** `:unpinned` is
`intropy deploy`'s job, not the developer's; reporting it as a placeholder would invite hand-editing an
image tag, which is exactly the discipline this toolchain enforces. It gets its own sentinel and the report

CLI knows only the tokens, the template knows what it emitted.

Validation comes free: the scan walks the *committed* tree, so a re-run that writes nothing still reports
"already onboarded, N placeholders left in M files".

The client has `CheckoutPaths` but nothing that switches branches:

```go

// Switch checks out an existing ref.

`Push(ctx, remote, "HEAD:refs/heads/"+branch)` already covers the push.

**The `ResetHard` hazard, stated once:** `gitops.refresh()` does `ResetHard(origin/<defaultBranch>)` then
`git clean -fdq`, and never switches branches. Leaving the checkout on a feature branch is *destructive* —
the next `gitops.Open` would reset that branch to `origin/main` and discard its commits. Restore the
default branch in a `defer`, **on success and on failure alike**.

`internal/deploy/publish.go`'s `Publish` is not reusable: it is hard-wired to `*Plan` and
`plan.RelKustomizationPath`, and its rebase-retry loop is for a one-line contended edit. `deploy init`

retry. Write a smaller `publishScaffold` alongside it.

`internal/deploy/init.go` — `Init(ctx, InitOptions) (*InitResult, error)`, sequenced:

1. Resolve the topology (slow, **no lock**).
2. `openSession(ctx, opts.session(), "git")` — no `kustomize`; nothing is built or diffed in the first cut.
3. Infer/validate `--domain`; read `deploy.yaml`, including `Platform` and the environment list.
4. Fetch templates at their pinned version, resolve values, render to staging — the host template once,
   the block template once per component.
5. `classifyStaged` against the live tree; `--plan` stops here.
6. Branch, write, commit, push, restore branch.

**Values contract.** `ResolveLayered` gets its first production caller (it has none today — left behind
when `manifests create` was deleted):

```go

values, err := template.ResolveLayered(tmpl, base, opts.Files, opts.Stdin, opts.SetValues, prompter)
if err != nil { return err }
if err := template.InjectReserved(tmpl, values, reserved); err != nil { return err }
```

Layering: schema defaults → derived facts → `-f` files → `--set` → prompts for missing required. Facts
beat defaults; the human beats facts. `seedDeclaredParams` **must** filter to declared parameters — an
undeclared key would sail past JSON Schema validation and land in the map anyway, which is how a template
silently acquires an undocumented dependency.

Seeded params: `name`, `kind`, `workload` (topology); `appId` (scaffold `values.appId`, else `name`);

Reserved injected keys: `topology` (the `InitModel`), `component` (this component's `InitComponent`, so the
skeleton needn't search), `gitops` (`{domain, system, component, registry, argocdAppNamespace,
environments[], platform{}}`), `scaffold` (the component's `.intropy/scaffold.json` values, or `{}`).

named topology components; default is the whole system, host included.

## Approved Plan:
# `intropy deploy init` — scaffold GitOps manifests from the topology

## Context

Onboarding a component into the GitOps repo is entirely manual today. `internal/gitops/layout.go`'s
`notFoundError` literally instructs the user to hand-create
`domains/<domain>/<system>/<component>/{component.yaml,base,overlays}`. Everything downstream is
automated — `intropy deploy` pins digests, `promote` copies them, `status`/`diff`/`sync` read ArgoCD — but
the tree itself is typed out by hand, per component, per environment, per customer.

`intropy manifests create` was an earlier attempt (added `f9fc2229`, removed `90dd4838` on 2026-07-26) and
failed for two recorded reasons: it rendered into `./deploy` **inside the component repo**, which nothing
consumes because ArgoCD reads the GitOps repo; and it pinned `newTag: latest`, contradicting the
digest-pinning discipline `deploy` exists to enforce. This design corrects both.

Outcome: after `intropy deploy init`, every file ArgoCD needs exists and every fact the CLI can derive is
filled in. What's left is a bounded, greppable list of placeholders — connection strings, hosts,
credentials, cron schedules — that only a human can supply. Complete manifests are explicitly a non-goal.

## What the existing customer repos already establish

Read from `~/dev/intropy/customers/*/gitops` — the design follows these rather than inventing conventions.

- **`scopes:` is already the convention** on every Dapr `Component`, listing the app-ids permitted to use it.
- **Dapr components belong in `base/`, identical across environments.** fluxia puts them per-overlay and
  varies the broker (`pubsub.in-memory` in dev, `pubsub.rabbitmq` in prod); that is a **deviation we are not
  following**. One broker type per system, one file, all environments. What legitimately differs per
  environment is the *credential*, not the component — and a Dapr `Component` references its secret by
  name (`secretKeyRef`), so identical YAML in `base/` resolves to different values in each environment's
  namespace. Overlays stay thin: `namespace`, `resources: [../../base]`, and the image pin `deploy` writes.
- **Extractors are `CronJob`s**, not Deployments — confirmed in both `fluxia/gitops/.../order-extractor`
  and `entrovia/gitops/.../order-extractor` and `entrovia/.../relex-fno`. Other blocks are Deployments.
- **The namespace is set by the overlay and not created by the customer repo.** fluxia uses a flat
  `namespace: integrations`; per my notes entrovia uses `{test,prod}-<slug>-integrations`, provisioned by
  `~/dev/intropy/platform/service-plane/gitops` along with Dapr itself, RabbitMQ, Vault and the
  `harbor-intropy-robot-credentials` / `rabbitmq-connection` secrets. **Customer repos must not install
  those.** So namespace is a parameter and `Namespace` objects are never emitted.
- **Image repositories differ per customer**: `harbor.intropy.io/fluxia/order-extractor` vs
  `harbor.intropy.io/integrations/int123`. The repo pattern is a parameter, not `<registry>/integrations/<name>`.
- **`system-host` is the only template with no Dockerfile** (extractor, loader, transactional and

(the arbitrary-owner pattern), and that `order-extractor/overlays/prod/pubsub.yaml` is `pubsub.in-memory`

## Decisions taken

| | |
|---|---|
| **Provider** | Repo-level `platform: {provider, pubsub, secretStore}` in `deploy.yaml`. One platform per repo, uniform across environments — no per-environment override. |
| **Write mode** | Create `deploy-init/<domain>-<system>`, commit only the staged paths, push the branch, restore the default branch. Never pushes to the default branch — a placeholder-bearing tree would be picked up by the ApplicationSet immediately. |
| **Scope** | Per-block tree **plus** a system-level directory for the system host, which owns the shared Dapr objects. |
| **Shared objects' owner** | The **system host** gets its own component directory. Exactly one Application owns each Dapr `Component`; `scopes:` lists the app-ids allowed to use it. |
| **Image-less directories** | New `kind: service` (default) / `kind: shared` on `component.yaml`; images required only for `service`. |
| **Conditionality** | `spec.files[]` with `when` in `template.yaml`. First match decides; an unmatched path is included, so every existing template renders byte-identically to today. |

### Why the host owns the shared objects

A Dapr `Component` is namespace-scoped, and all of a customer's integrations share one namespace. So
`metadata.name: pubsub` is a single Kubernetes object for the whole namespace and exactly one ArgoCD
Application may own it. `scopes:` controls which app-ids may *use* the component; it does not change the
name, so it does not prevent the collision — it is the right complement to single ownership, not a
substitute for it (fluxia's table above is what "scopes without single ownership" looks like).

Putting them in the host directory rather than an invented `shared/` means the gitops tree mirrors the
code layout and reuses a name that already exists in the topology and in `.intropy/scaffold.json`
(`RoleSystemHost`). The host has no Dockerfile and therefore no image, which is exactly what `kind: shared`
describes.

Kustomize *would* let each block reference the host directory via `resources: [../../../host/base]` — the
repo already relies on upward traversal for `../../base`. It is the wrong tool here: N blocks referencing
it means N Applications rendering and claiming the same object, and
`internal/kustomize/manifest.go` builds each overlay and diffs the rendered stream, so the shared objects
would appear inside every block's `deploy diff`. No reference is needed anyway — a Dapr `Component` is not
a kustomize dependency of a Deployment; the sidecar resolves it by name through the Dapr control plane at
runtime. Ordering, if it ever matters, is an ArgoCD sync-wave annotation on the host directory.

## Target tree

```
domains/sales/ordersync/
  host/                                 kind: shared — no image, nothing to pin
    component.yaml
    base/
      kustomization.yaml
      dapr/pubsub.yaml                  in-memory | rabbitmq | servicebus — one per repo platform
      dapr/secretstore.yaml
      dapr/binding-<connector>.yaml     one per topology connector, when connectors exist
      secrets/secrets.yaml              REPLACE-ME-* stubs, referenced by secretKeyRef
    overlays/dev/kustomization.yaml     namespace: <parameter>, resources: [../../base]
    overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml    identical but for the namespace
    README.md                            what each placeholder is and where to get it
  order-extract/                        kind: service — extractor ⇒ CronJob
    component.yaml
    base/{cronjob.yaml,kustomization.yaml}
    overlays/{dev,prod}/kustomization.yaml
  order-load/                           kind: service — loader ⇒ Deployment
    component.yaml
    base/{deployment.yaml,kustomization.yaml}
    overlays/{dev,prod}/kustomization.yaml
```

No `Namespace` object anywhere — the service-plane provisions it. Images are left at the `:unpinned`
sentinel; `intropy deploy` is the only thing that pins. Because the environment comes from the
ApplicationSet's cluster generator rather than the path (see step 3), the host directory needs an overlay
for **every** environment in `deploy.yaml`, not a subset.

### 1. Conditional file filter in `internal/template`

`internal/template/manifest.go` — add to `Spec`:

```go
// FileRule conditionally includes part of a skeleton. Path is a slash-separated
// glob relative to skeleton/, matched against the *source* path with any .tmpl
// suffix included; a trailing "/**" also matches everything beneath the
// directory. When is a Go template (sprig available) rendered against the
// resolved values; any result other than "", "false" or "0" includes the match.
// The first rule whose Path matches decides, and a path no rule matches is
// included — so a template without spec.files renders exactly as before.
type FileRule struct {
    Path string `yaml:"path" json:"path"`
    When string `yaml:"when" json:"when"`
}
```

Three obligations that are easy to miss:

- `Files` must also be added to the **shadow `rawSpec` struct inside `Spec.UnmarshalYAML`**
  (`manifest.go:66`) — it decodes into `rawSpec`, so a field added only to `Spec` is silently dropped.
- `validate()` rejects an empty `path`, rejects an empty `when` (a rule with no condition is an authoring
  error), and **pre-parses each `when`** so a syntax error surfaces at `LoadTemplate`, not mid-render.
- Matching is against the **source** path, not the rendered one: a rule that decides on values cannot
  depend on a path values produce. Document that a `{{ .name }}/` segment is only reachable via a glob.

New `internal/template/filter.go`:

```go
type skeletonFilter struct {
    rules  []FileRule
    values map[string]any
    cache  map[int]bool // a when depends only on values — evaluate each rule once
}
func newSkeletonFilter(rules []FileRule, values map[string]any) *skeletonFilter
func (f *skeletonFilter) include(rel string) (bool, error)
func matchSkeletonPath(pattern, rel string) bool
func truthy(rendered string) bool
```

`include` evaluates `when` with the **existing `renderExpr` (`internal/template/values.go:220`)** — no new
expression language. `renderExpr` sets `Option("missingkey=error")`, so a typo'd value name is a loud
error rather than a silent skip. Booleans are real booleans by then (`coerceKnownFieldValue`), so
`{{ .externalSecrets }}` renders `true`/`false`.

`internal/template/render.go` — extract the walk:

```go
func RenderFiltered(srcDir, destDir string, values map[string]any, rules []FileRule) error
func Render(srcDir, destDir string, values map[string]any) error {
    return RenderFiltered(srcDir, destDir, values, nil)
}
```

In the existing `WalkDir` callback, right after `rel` is computed and **before** `renderPath`:

```go
rel = filepath.ToSlash(rel)
include, err := filter.include(rel)
if err != nil { return err }
if !include {
    if d.IsDir() { return fs.SkipDir }
    return nil
}
```

`int create` and the dependency path keep calling `Render` and are provably unaffected.

**Tests** (`internal/template/filter_test.go` plus additions to `render_test.go`) — string constants and
`t.TempDir()`, per `CONTRIBUTING.md`:

- No rules → everything rendered. The regression guard for `int create`.
- `when` true → present; false → absent.
- `dapr/**` false → whole subtree absent, **and a file inside it with a deliberately malformed template
  body does not fail the render**. This proves pruning happens before parsing; an implementation that
  filters after walking fails it.
- First-match-wins with two overlapping rules.
- `when` referencing an undefined value → error.
- Truthiness table: `""`/`"false"`/`"0"` excluded; `"true"`/`"1"`/`"yes"` included.
- `LoadTemplate` rejects empty `path`, empty `when`, malformed `{{`.
- `Spec.UnmarshalYAML` preserves `files` — the shadow-struct trap.

### 2. `InjectReserved` in `internal/template`

Param types are scalar-only (`fieldFromSchema`, `manifest.go:150`); widening them would ripple through
`coerce`, `Fields`, `AutoPrompter`, `applySetValues`, `--set` syntax and the dashboard form code. **Do not
widen them.** Promote the deleted command's one good idea — reserved keys injected *after* schema
validation — into a shared helper:

```go
// internal/template/values.go
const (
    ReservedTopologyKey  = "topology"
    ReservedComponentKey = "component"
    ReservedGitopsKey    = "gitops"
    ReservedScaffoldKey  = "scaffold"
)

// InjectReserved adds structured, non-parameter data to a resolved value map
// after JSON Schema validation, so a skeleton can range over data that is not
// expressible as a scalar parameter. It refuses any key that collides with a
// declared parameter or a spec.values entry.
func InjectReserved(t *Template, values map[string]any, reserved map[string]any) error
```

This is what makes the list-shaped work possible with no further renderer change: **which files exist** is
`when` over the injected structure (`when: '{{ gt (len .topology.connectors) 0 }}'`); **multiplicity
inside a file** is `range` into a multi-document YAML. Multi-doc over per-item files is deliberate —
kustomize handles it natively, zero renderer extension, and "we added a connector" is a one-file diff.

Tests: reserved key colliding with a param → error; colliding with a `spec.values` entry → error;
injection lands after validation, so a reserved value that would fail the schema still works.

### 6. The deployment model — `internal/deploy/initmodel.go`

```go
// InitModel is the topology view the manifest skeletons see under the reserved
// "topology" key: derived, flattened and sorted. Raw topology.Topology is
// unsuitable — its APIs/Provides/Consumes are json.RawMessage, and neither map
// iteration nor host emission order is stable, which idempotent rendering requires.
type InitModel struct {
    System     string          `json:"system"`
    Host       InitHost        `json:"host"`       // name, appIds it must scope
    Components []InitComponent `json:"components"` // name, kind, appId, workload, topics, connectors
    PubSubs    []InitPubSub    `json:"pubsubs"`    // name + the sorted app-ids to put in scopes:
    Topics     []InitTopic     `json:"topics"`
    Connectors []InitConnector `json:"connectors"` // name, externalSystem, transport, directions, appIds
}
func newInitModel(t *topology.Topology, scaffolds []template.ScaffoldEntry) InitModel
```

`InitComponent.Workload` is `"cronjob"` for `kind == extractor` and `"deployment"` otherwise, matching what
fluxia and entrovia already do. That drives the base file swap via `when`, and it is the single most
valuable thing the topology contributes.

`InitPubSub.AppIDs` is the union of a topic's `Publishers` and `Subscribers` mapped to app-ids — this is
what populates `scopes:`, so the emitted Component grants exactly the blocks the topology says use it.
`InitConnector.AppIDs` does the same from `Connector.UsedBy`.

Sorting everything is load-bearing: idempotency depends on byte-identical re-renders, and neither Go map
order nor host emission order is guaranteed. Inject via a JSON round-trip into `map[string]any` so `index`
and sprig behave uniformly.

Tests from a string-constant topology JSON: extractor → cronjob and loader → deployment; pubsub app-ids
are the sorted union of publishers and subscribers; connectors deduped and sorted; `appId` falls back to
`name`; an unwired component survives.

Never `Render` straight into the tree: `writeAtomically` overwrites, and an overlay contains digests
`deploy` pinned. Render to a fresh staging temp dir, then classify per file.

```go
type fileAction struct {
    Rel    string // repo-relative, slash-separated
    Action string // "create" | "identical" | "skip-exists" | "overwrite"
}
func classifyStaged(stagingDir, destRoot string, force bool) ([]fileAction, error)
func applyStaged(stagingDir, destRoot string, actions []fileAction) error
```

- Fresh onboarding → all `create`.
- Byte-identical existing file → `identical`; not written, not reported as a change.
- Differing existing file → `skip-exists` (reported, not written) unless `--force` → `overwrite`.
- Topology grew a component → only that subtree is `create`; existing components untouched.
  **Additive by default** is what makes this safe to re-run for the system's whole life.
- `--force` **guard**: refuse outright, naming the files, if any target `overlays/<env>/kustomization.yaml`
  carries an `images:` entry with a digest — overwriting that un-deploys production. Read it with the
  existing `kustomize.ReadKustomization`.
- `--plan` prints the actions and returns before `applyStaged`.

`template.EnsureOutputDir` is bypassed — its "refuse a non-empty directory" policy is wrong here;
`classifyStaged` owns the policy.

digest; nothing written if any classification errors.

`internal/deploy/init.go` — `Init(ctx, InitOptions) (*InitResult, error)`, sequenced:

1. Resolve the topology (slow, **no lock**).
2. `openSession(ctx, opts.session(), "git")` — no `kustomize`; nothing is built or diffed in the first cut.
3. Infer/validate `--domain`; read `deploy.yaml`, including `Platform` and the environment list.
4. Fetch templates at their pinned version, resolve values, render to staging — the host template once,

```go

values, err := template.ResolveLayered(tmpl, base, opts.Files, opts.Stdin, opts.SetValues, prompter)
if err != nil { return err }
if err := template.InjectReserved(tmpl, values, reserved); err != nil { return err }

beat defaults; the human beats facts. `seedDeclaredParams` **must** filter to declared parameters — an

Reserved injected keys: `topology` (the `InitModel`), `component` (this component's `InitComponent`, so the

| `--system` | Override the topology's `system` as the GitOps system segment |

- **`deploy-component/`** — the per-block tier. `base/cronjob.yaml.tmpl` vs `base/deployment.yaml.tmpl`

Top-level rather than the deleted design's `<template>/manifests/` subtree — that failed because not every

which block template it came from. Delete any surviving dead `manifests/` directories. Cut a release tag;

**The cross-repo ordering hazard — the single largest risk here.** `LoadTemplate` uses plain
`yaml.Unmarshal`, **not** `KnownFields(true)`. An older CLI reading a template that uses `spec.files`
therefore silently ignores the filter and **renders every file** — Azure manifests into a beebyte repo. A
silent wrong answer. Containment is structural rather than a version check: `deploy-host` and
`deploy-component` are fetched only by `deploy init`, which exists only in a CLI that understands
`spec.files`. Hence the rule: **no pre-existing template may adopt `spec.files` until the CLI floor
moves.** Enforce it in the templates repo review checklist; optionally add
`metadata.labels["intropy.dev/minimum-cli-version"]`, checked by `deploy init`, as belt-and-braces.

## Verification

Unit and integration, following `CONTRIBUTING.md` — string-constant fixtures, `t.TempDir()`, no golden
files, no network:

- `go test ./internal/template/...` — the filter suite, especially the malformed-body-in-a-pruned-subtree
  case, plus every pre-existing `render_test.go`/`create_test.go`/`dependencies_test.go` test unchanged.
- `go test ./internal/gitops/...` — `platform` merge semantics, `kind` defaulting and validation, and every
  existing `gitopstest` fixture still parsing.
- `go test ./internal/topology/... ./internal/dashboard/...` — the moved graph runner; dashboard tests
  passing untouched via the existing `topologyProvider` stub.
- `go test ./internal/deploy/...` — `init_test.go` end to end: `gitopstest.NewRepo` for the GitOps side,
  `httptest` + in-memory `buildTarGz` with the test-only `Owner`/`Repo`/`GitHubBaseURL`/`HTTP` override
  fields for the templates side (copy `internal/template/create_test.go`), a `--topology` JSON string
  constant so no dotnet runs, and a `command.Runner` stub for git. Cases: fresh onboarding produces the
  expected path set including the host directory; extractor gets a CronJob and loader a Deployment; the
  Dapr components land in `base/` exactly once and every overlay differs only by `namespace`; `scopes:`
  matches the topology's publishers and subscribers; re-run is a no-op; a newly added topology component is created
  incrementally; `--plan` writes nothing and touches no git; `deploy` refuses the `kind: shared`
  directory with the precise message; placeholders reported; JSON shape; the branch is created, pushed,
  **and the checkout is restored to the default branch even on failure**.
- `go test ./cmd/intropy/...` — registration under `deploy`, `init` winning over the component argument,
  flag validation and usage exit code 2, completions silent without config.

Manual end-to-end, once the template release is cut — run against a scratch branch of a real customer repo:

```bash
# 1. capture a topology once, so iteration doesn't pay for a dotnet build each time
cd <a system workspace>
dotnet run --project ./<X>.SystemHost -- graph > /tmp/topo.json

# 2. dry run — writes nothing, touches no git
intropy deploy init --domain sales --topology /tmp/topo.json --plan

# 3. for real, then read the branch as a reviewer would
intropy deploy init --domain sales --topology /tmp/topo.json
# in a clone of the gitops repo, on the pushed branch:
kustomize build domains/sales/<system>/<host>/overlays/dev          # must build
kustomize build domains/sales/<system>/<block>/overlays/dev         # must build
grep -rn 'REPLACE-ME-' domains/sales/<system>/                      # matches the reported table
# exactly one Component/pubsub owner across the system, and its scopes
# list the app-ids the topology says publish or subscribe:
grep -rn -A3 'name: pubsub' domains/sales/<system>/

# 4. idempotency and the guard
intropy deploy init --domain sales --topology /tmp/topo.json    # all "identical", nothing written
intropy deploy <block> --env dev                                 # pins a digest
intropy deploy init --domain sales --topology /tmp/topo.json --force  # must REFUSE, naming the file
intropy deploy <host> --env dev                                  # must refuse: kind "shared"

# 5. conditionality — render with pubsub servicebus vs rabbitmq and diff the file sets
```

Compare the result against `~/dev/intropy/customers/fluxia/gitops/domains/orders/order-flow/order-extractor`,
which is the closest hand-written example, and treat any structural difference as either a template bug or
a convention worth adopting.

## Out of the first cut

- **Fix fluxia's duplicate `Component/pubsub` owners** and the in-memory-across-two-pods prod component.
  Separate remediation, but `deploy init`'s single-owner rule is what stops it recurring.
- `intropy sys graph -o topology.json`, which makes `--topology` free in CI.
- `deploy init --check` exiting non-zero on remaining placeholders; surfacing the count in `deploy status`;
  and (a real safety win, but a behaviour change to `deploy`, so a separate decision) having
  `intropy deploy` **refuse** an overlay whose component tree still contains placeholders.
- `intropy gitops init` for `deploy.yaml` + ApplicationSet bootstrap — cannot be a `deploy` subcommand,
  since every one of them refuses a repo without `deploy.yaml`.
- A `deploy.yaml` `imageRepoPattern` key, once the fluxia-vs-entrovia naming difference is reconciled, so
  `imageRepo` stops needing a prompt.
- ArgoCD sync-wave annotation on the host directory, if Dapr sidecar retry proves insufficient.
- `spec.files[].forEach` per-item fan-out, if multi-doc YAML ever proves insufficient.
- Extending an existing `component.yaml`'s `environments` when `deploy.yaml` grows one.

## Open questions worth answering during implementation

1. **Host directory name — assumed `host`.** The ApplicationSet name is
   `<domain>-<system>-<component>-<cluster>`, so `host` yields `sales-ordersync-host-dev`, whereas the
   scaffold's own `values.name` would give the redundant `sales-ordersync-ordersync-host-dev`. Going with
   `host` unless you prefer otherwise. Worth also checking whether the ApplicationSet needs to *exclude*
   the host directory from any image-related automation.
2. **Secrets mechanism** — plain `Secret` stubs with base64 placeholders, `ExternalSecret` (external-secrets
   operator), Vault (which my notes say the service-plane already installs), or sealed-secrets? This
   decides what `deploy-host` emits and whether a placeholder is even legal to commit.
3. **Does the service-plane already provide a namespace-wide `pubsub` Component?** If Dapr, RabbitMQ and the
   `rabbitmq-connection` secret are all service-plane-provisioned, the pub/sub Component may belong there
   too — in which case `deploy-host` should emit only *bindings* and secrets, and reference the
   platform's pub/sub by name. Verify against `~/dev/intropy/platform/service-plane/gitops`
   and `docs/multi-tenancy.md` before writing the host template.
4. **Confirm the ApplicationSet generator shape** with one `grep -rn 'path.segments' <gitops-repo>`. The
   design infers a directories generator globbing `domains/*/*/*` matrix'd against clusters, from the name
   template recorded in `Coordinate.AppName`'s doc comment. If it instead keys on `component.yaml`, `kind`
   is what keeps the host directory visible — the design still holds, but confirm.
5. **`int201`-style integration ids** appear in customer trees (`INT123`, `int999`) but in neither the
   topology nor the scaffold record. If manifest labels or directory names must carry them, where does
   `deploy init` get them?
6. `deploy-host`/`deploy-component` will appear in `int create`'s template completions — accept the wart,
   or filter on an `intropy.dev/template-kind: deploy` label?
7. Is `REPLACE-ME-<HINT>` acceptable, or is there already a convention in the customer repos to match?

---
name: project-dapr-uniform-across-envs
description: Dapr component config must be identical in every environment and live in base/; fluxia's per-overlay broker split is a deviation
metadata:
  type: project
---

Dapr `Component` manifests belong in a system's `base/` and must be **identical
across all environments**. One broker type per system, one file. Confirmed by
Robin on 2026-07-28 when reviewing the `intropy deploy init` design.

`~/dev/intropy/customers/fluxia/gitops` is a **deviation, not a convention**: it
puts `pubsub.yaml` in each `overlays/<env>/` and varies the broker
(`pubsub.in-memory` in dev, `pubsub.rabbitmq` in prod). Do not copy it, and do
not cite it as precedent.

**Why:** what legitimately differs per environment is the *credential*, not the
component. A Dapr Component reaches its secret via `secretKeyRef`, so identical
YAML in `base/` resolves to different values in each environment's namespace.
Varying the component itself makes dev and prod structurally different for no
gain.

**How to apply:** overlays stay thin — `namespace:`, `resources: [../../base]`,
and the image pin `intropy deploy` writes. Never add a per-environment
`platform:` override to `deploy.yaml`; the repo-level block is deliberate.
Related: [[project-gitops-manifest-conventions]]

---
name: project-gitops-manifest-conventions
description: Kubernetes manifest conventions observed across customers/*/gitops — workload kind per block, scopes, namespace and image-repo variance
metadata:

Observed 2026-07-28 across `~/dev/intropy/customers/*/gitops`, while designing
`intropy deploy init` (plan: `~/.claude/plans/i-want-to-be-splendid-taco.md`).
None of this is derivable from intropy-cli's own code.

- **Extractors are `CronJob`s, other blocks are `Deployment`s.** Confirmed in
  fluxia `orders/order-flow/order-extractor`, entrovia `orders/order-flow/order-extractor`
  and entrovia `scm/order-proposals/relex-fno`.
- **`scopes:` on every Dapr Component** lists the app-ids allowed to use it. It
  does *not* change `metadata.name`, so it does not prevent two Applications
  owning the same Component — it complements single ownership, never substitutes.
- **Namespaces are set by the overlay and never created by the customer repo.**
  fluxia uses a flat `integrations`; entrovia uses `{test,prod}-<slug>-integrations`
  provisioned by `~/dev/intropy/platform/service-plane/gitops`. So namespace is a
  parameter, and customer repos emit no `Namespace` object.
- **Image repositories differ per customer**: `harbor.intropy.io/fluxia/order-extractor`
  vs `harbor.intropy.io/integrations/int123`. There is no single derivable pattern.
- **`system-host` is the only template with no Dockerfile**, so the system host has
  no image — it is a composition root, not a deployed container.
- **Live bug:** fluxia has two Applications both owning `Component/pubsub` in
  namespace `integrations` (`order-management/INT123/overlays/dev` and
  `orders/order-flow/order-extractor/overlays/dev`), and the extractor's *prod*
  component is `pubsub.in-memory` scoped to two app-ids, which cannot work across
  pods.

**Why:** these conventions are what generated manifests must match, and several
of them contradict what the CLI's own layout code would suggest.

**How to apply:** check a real customer repo before treating any manifest shape as
canonical, and treat differences between customers as parameters rather than
picking one. Related: [[project-dapr-uniform-across-envs]]

16	// topologyProvider fetches the declared topologies for the workspace. Each
17	// entry's Path is the on-disk system directory (the handler normalizes it to
18	// a root-relative identifier). Per-host failures are returned as messages
19	// alongside the successes so one broken host cannot hide the rest.
20	type topologyProvider func(ctx context.Context) (entries []topology.Entry, errs []string)
21	
22	// graphTimeout bounds one host's graph verb. It is generous because the first
23	// `dotnet run` restores and builds the project before the verb executes.
24	const graphTimeout = 5 * time.Minute
25	
26	// stderrTailBytes bounds how much of a failing host's stderr is echoed into
27	// the error message shown in the dashboard.
28	const stderrTailBytes = 2048
29	
30	// hostGraphProvider returns the default provider: it finds every scaffolded
31	// system host under root and asks each one to print its declared topology via
32	// `dotnet run --project <host> -- graph`. The verb's contract is JSON only on
33	// stdout (logs on stderr); hosts scaffolded before the graph verb existed
34	// simply fail, which surfaces as an error the UI renders.
35	func hostGraphProvider(root string) topologyProvider {
36		return func(ctx context.Context) ([]topology.Entry, []string) {
37			hosts, _ := template.ListScaffolds(root)
38			var entries []topology.Entry
39			var errs []string
40			for _, h := range hosts {
41				if h.Role != template.RoleSystemHost {
42					continue
43				}
44				t, err := runGraphVerb(ctx, h.Path)
45				if err != nil {
46					errs = append(errs, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %v", displayPath(root, h.Path), err))
47					continue
48				}
49				// The system directory is the workspace directory holding the
50				// host: components are scaffolded as its siblings.
51				entries = append(entries, topology.Entry{Path: filepath.Dir(h.Path), Topology: *t})
52			}
53			return entries, errs
54		}
55	}
56	
57	// runGraphVerb executes one host's graph verb and decodes its stdout. It
58	// builds first and then runs with --no-build --no-launch-profile — the
59	// invocation the topology library documents — because a plain `dotnet run`
60	// writes build and launch-profile messages to stdout, corrupting the JSON.
61	func runGraphVerb(ctx context.Context, hostDir string) (*topology.Topology, error) {
62		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, graphTimeout)
63		defer cancel()
64	
65		build := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "dotnet", "build", hostDir, "-v", "q")
66		var buildOut bytes.Buffer
67		build.Stdout, build.Stderr = &buildOut, &buildOut
68		if err := build.Run(); err != nil {
69			return nil, fmt.Errorf("build failed: %v%s", err, tail(buildOut.Bytes()))
70		}
71	
72		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "dotnet", "run", "--no-build", "--no-launch-profile", "--project", hostDir, "--", "graph")
73		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
74		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
75		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
76			return nil, fmt.Errorf("graph verb failed: %v%s", err, tail(stderr.Bytes()))
77		}
78		t, err := topology.Decode(&stdout)
79		if err != nil {
80			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w%s", err, tail(stdout.Bytes()))
81		}
82		return t, nil
83	}
84	
85	// displayPath shortens a host directory to its root-relative form for error
86	// messages, matching the identifier space the rest of the API uses.
87	func displayPath(root, p string) string {
88		if rel, err := filepath.Rel(root, p); err == nil {
89			return filepath.ToSlash(rel)
90		}
91		return filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Clean(p))
92	}
93	
94	// tail formats the last stderrTailBytes of a command stream for inclusion in
95	// an error message, or nothing when the stream is empty.
96	func tail(b []byte) string {
97		s := strings.TrimSpace(string(b))
98		if s == "" {
99			return ""
100		}
101		if len(s) > stderrTailBytes {
102			s = "…" + s[len(s)-stderrTailBytes:]
103		}
104		return ": " + s
105	}

1	// Package topology models the declared system topology an integration
2	// system's host emits. The record declares the system's shape: its components
3	// (blocks) and the wiring between them, expressed inline on each component —
4	// the topics it subscribes to and publishes on, the API contracts it provides
5	// and consumes, and the external connectors it uses. Top-level topics[] and
6	// connectors[] sections carry the shared metadata (contracts, transports,
7	// external systems) those inline references point at.
8	//
9	// The CLI never derives a topology itself: the system host's `graph` verb
10	// prints the record — JSON only, on stdout — and consumers decode that stream.
11	package topology
12	
13	import (
14		"encoding/json"
15		"fmt"
16		"io"
17	)
18	
19	const (
20		// APIVersion is the topology schema this CLI understands. A record with
21		// any other apiVersion is an error, not a guess.
22		APIVersion = "topology.intropy.io/v1"
23	
24		// Kind is the expected document kind under APIVersion.
25		Kind = "SystemTopology"
26	)
27	
28	// Topology is one system's declared graph. Wiring is inlined on each component
29	// rather than kept in a separate edge list: a component names the topics it
30	// subscribes to and publishes on and the connectors it uses. The top-level
31	// Topics and Connectors sections are lookup tables the inline references
32	// resolve against (contract, transport, external system).
33	type Topology struct {
34		APIVersion string      `json:"apiVersion"`
35		Kind       string      `json:"kind,omitempty"`
36		System     string      `json:"system"`
37		Components []Component `json:"components,omitempty"`
38		Topics     []Topic     `json:"topics,omitempty"`
39		Connectors []Connector `json:"connectors,omitempty"`
40		Contracts  []Contract  `json:"contracts,omitempty"`
41		// APIs, and each component's Provides/Consumes below, are the contract
42		// (request/response) surfaces. Their element shape is not yet finalized,
43		// so they are parsed opaquely: preserved for round-tripping to the
44		// frontend without asserting a schema the CLI does not yet render.
45		APIs []json.RawMessage `json:"apis,omitempty"`
46	}
47	
48	// Component is a deployable block of the system. Kind is the block type
49	// (extractor, loader, transactionalIntegration, …). A component's directory,
50	// which joins it to its .intropy/scaffold.json project, is its Name relative
51	// to the system root.
52	type Component struct {
53		Name       string         `json:"name"`
54		Kind       string         `json:"kind"`
55		Subscribes []TopicRef     `json:"subscribes,omitempty"`
56		Publishes  []Publication  `json:"publishes,omitempty"`
57		Connectors []ConnectorUse `json:"connectors,omitempty"`
58		// Provides/Consumes are contract surfaces, parsed opaquely (see APIs).
59		Provides []json.RawMessage `json:"provides,omitempty"`
60		Consumes []json.RawMessage `json:"consumes,omitempty"`
61	}
62	
63	// TopicRef is a component's subscription to a pub/sub topic.
64	type TopicRef struct {
65		PubSub string `json:"pubsub"`
66		Topic  string `json:"topic"`
67	}
68	
69	// Publication is a component's output onto a pub/sub topic. Port names the
70	// component output the message leaves through.
71	type Publication struct {
72		Port   string `json:"port,omitempty"`
73		PubSub string `json:"pubsub"`
74		Topic  string `json:"topic"`
75	}
76	
77	// ConnectorUse is a component's use of an external connector. Direction is
78	// "in" (external → component) or "out" (component → external).
79	type ConnectorUse struct {
80		Connector string `json:"connector"`
81		Direction string `json:"direction"`
82	}
83	
84	// Topic is a declared pub/sub topic: the metadata for a (PubSub, Topic) pair
85	// components reference. Contract is the message contract it carries;
86	// Publishers/Subscribers name the components on each end.
87	type Topic struct {
88		PubSub      string   `json:"pubsub"`
89		Topic       string   `json:"topic"`
90		Contract    string   `json:"contract,omitempty"`
91		Publishers  []string `json:"publishers,omitempty"`
92		Subscribers []string `json:"subscribers,omitempty"`
93	}
94	
95	// Contract is a message contract in the system's registry, keyed by Name —
96	// the same fully-qualified type name Topic.Contract references. ShortName is
97	// the bare type name (the join key to a scaffold record's values.contract).
98	// Schema is the contract's JSON Schema as the host emitted it; the CLI passes
99	// it through to the frontend without interpreting it. Fingerprint identifies
100	// the schema shape (a hash over its canonical form), so equal fingerprints
101	// mean equal shapes across systems.
102	type Contract struct {
103		Name        string          `json:"name"`
104		Kind        string          `json:"kind,omitempty"`
105		ShortName   string          `json:"shortName,omitempty"`
106		MediaType   string          `json:"mediaType,omitempty"`
107		Fingerprint string          `json:"fingerprint,omitempty"`
108		Schema      json.RawMessage `json:"schema,omitempty"`
109	}
110	
111	// Transport describes how a connector moves data. SupportsInput/SupportsOutput
112	// declare the directions the transport itself can carry.
113	type Transport struct {
114		Type           string `json:"type"`
115		SupportsInput  bool   `json:"supportsInput"`
116		SupportsOutput bool   `json:"supportsOutput"`
117	}
118	
119	// Connector is an external system integration point. ExternalSystem is the
120	// system it fronts, Directions the directions it is wired in, and UsedBy the
121	// components that use it.
122	type Connector struct {
123		Name           string    `json:"name"`
124		ExternalSystem string    `json:"externalSystem,omitempty"`
125		Transport      Transport `json:"transport"`
126		Directions     []string  `json:"directions,omitempty"`
127		UsedBy         []string  `json:"usedBy,omitempty"`
128	}
129	
130	// Entry is one system's topology plus the workspace directory it belongs to,
131	// flattened into one self-describing JSON document for the API.
132	type Entry struct {
133		Path string `json:"path"`
134		Topology
135	}
136	
137	// Decode parses a topology record from r (typically a host `graph` verb's
138	// stdout). A record whose apiVersion this CLI does not understand is an
139	// error, not a guess. Callers wrap the error with the record's origin.
140	func Decode(r io.Reader) (*Topology, error) {
141		var t Topology
142		if err := json.NewDecoder(r).Decode(&t); err != nil {
143			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse topology record: %w", err)
144		}
145		if t.APIVersion != APIVersion {
146			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported topology apiVersion %q (this CLI understands %q)",
147				t.APIVersion, APIVersion)
148		}
149		return &t, nil
150	}

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/robinhultman/.claude/skills/golang-cli

**Persona:** You are a Go CLI engineer. You build tools that feel native to the Unix shell — composable, scriptable, and predictable under automation.

**Modes:**

- **Build** — creating a new CLI from scratch: follow the project structure, root command setup, flag binding, and version embedding sections sequentially.
- **Extend** — adding subcommands, flags, or completions to an existing CLI: read the current command tree first, then apply changes consistent with the existing structure.
- **Review** — auditing an existing CLI for correctness: check the Common Mistakes table, verify `SilenceUsage`/`SilenceErrors`, flag-to-Viper binding, exit codes, and stdout/stderr discipline.

# Go CLI Best Practices

Use Cobra + Viper as the default stack for Go CLI applications. Cobra provides the command/subcommand/flag structure and Viper handles configuration from files, environment variables, and flags with automatic layering. This combination powers kubectl, docker, gh, hugo, and most production Go CLIs.

When using Cobra or Viper, refer to the library's official documentation and code examples for current API signatures.

For trivial single-purpose tools with no subcommands and few flags, stdlib `flag` is sufficient.

## Quick Reference

| Concern             | Package / Tool                       |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Commands & flags    | `github.com/spf13/cobra`             |
| Configuration       | `github.com/spf13/viper`             |
| Flag parsing        | `github.com/spf13/pflag` (via Cobra) |
| Colored output      | `github.com/fatih/color`             |
| Table output        | `github.com/olekukonko/tablewriter`  |
| Interactive prompts | `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` |
| Version injection   | `go build -ldflags`                  |
| Distribution        | `goreleaser`                         |

## Project Structure

Organize CLI commands in `cmd/myapp/` with one file per command. Keep `main.go` minimal — it only calls `Execute()`.

```
myapp/
├── cmd/
│   └── myapp/
│       ├── main.go              # package main, only calls Execute()
│       ├── root.go              # Root command + Viper init
│       ├── serve.go             # "serve" subcommand
│       ├── migrate.go           # "migrate" subcommand
│       └── version.go           # "version" subcommand
├── go.mod
└── go.sum
```

`main.go` should be minimal — see [assets/examples/main.go](assets/examples/main.go).

## Root Command Setup

The root command initializes Viper configuration and sets up global behavior via `PersistentPreRunE`. See [assets/examples/root.go](assets/examples/root.go).

Key points:

- `SilenceUsage: true` MUST be set — prevents printing the full usage text on every error
- `SilenceErrors: true` MUST be set — lets you control error output format yourself
- `PersistentPreRunE` runs before every subcommand, so config is always initialized
- Logs go to stderr, output goes to stdout

## Subcommands

Add subcommands by creating separate files in `cmd/myapp/` and registering them in `init()`. See [assets/examples/serve.go](assets/examples/serve.go) for a complete subcommand example including command groups.

## Flags

See [assets/examples/flags.go](assets/examples/flags.go) for all flag patterns:

### Persistent vs Local

- **Persistent** flags are inherited by all subcommands (e.g., `--config`)
- **Local** flags only apply to the command they're defined on (e.g., `--port`)

### Required Flags

Use `MarkFlagRequired`, `MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive`, and `MarkFlagsOneRequired` for flag constraints.

### Flag Validation with RegisterFlagCompletionFunc

Provide completion suggestions for flag values.

### Always Bind Flags to Viper

This ensures `viper.GetInt("port")` returns the flag value, env var `MYAPP_PORT`, or config file value — whichever has highest precedence.

## Argument Validation

Cobra provides built-in validators for positional arguments. See [assets/examples/args.go](assets/examples/args.go) for both built-in and custom validation examples.

| Validator                   | Description                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `cobra.NoArgs`              | Fails if any args provided           |
| `cobra.ExactArgs(n)`        | Requires exactly n args              |
| `cobra.MinimumNArgs(n)`     | Requires at least n args             |
| `cobra.MaximumNArgs(n)`     | Allows at most n args                |
| `cobra.RangeArgs(min, max)` | Requires between min and max         |
| `cobra.ExactValidArgs(n)`   | Exactly n args, must be in ValidArgs |

## Configuration with Viper

Viper resolves configuration values in this order (highest to lowest precedence):

1. **CLI flags** (explicit user input)
2. **Environment variables** (deployment config)
3. **Config file** (persistent settings)
4. **Defaults** (set in code)

See [assets/examples/config.go](assets/examples/config.go) for complete Viper integration including struct unmarshaling and config file watching.

### Example Config File (.myapp.yaml)

```yaml
port: 8080
host: localhost
log-level: info
database:
  dsn: postgres://localhost:5432/myapp
  max-conn: 25
```

With the setup above, these are all equivalent:

- Flag: `--port 9090`
- Env var: `MYAPP_PORT=9090`
- Config file: `port: 9090`

## Version and Build Info

Version SHOULD be embedded at compile time using `ldflags`. See [assets/examples/version.go](assets/examples/version.go) for the version command and build instructions.

## Exit Codes

Exit codes MUST follow Unix conventions:

| Code  | Meaning           | When to Use                               |
| ----- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| 0     | Success           | Operation completed normally              |
| 1     | General error     | Runtime failure                           |
| 2     | Usage error       | Invalid flags or arguments                |
| 64-78 | BSD sysexits      | Specific error categories                 |
| 126   | Cannot execute    | Permission denied                         |
| 127   | Command not found | Missing dependency                        |
| 128+N | Signal N          | Terminated by signal (e.g., 130 = SIGINT) |

See [assets/examples/exit_codes.go](assets/examples/exit_codes.go) for a pattern mapping errors to exit codes.

## I/O Patterns

See [assets/examples/output.go](assets/examples/output.go) for all I/O patterns:

- **stdout vs stderr**: NEVER write diagnostic output to stdout — stdout is for program output (pipeable), stderr for logs/errors/diagnostics
- **Detecting pipe vs terminal**: check `os.ModeCharDevice` on stdout
- **Machine-readable output**: support `--output` flag for table/json/plain formats
- **Colors**: use `fatih/color` which auto-disables when output is not a terminal

## Signal Handling

Signal handling MUST use `signal.NotifyContext` to propagate cancellation through context. See [assets/examples/signal.go](assets/examples/signal.go) for graceful HTTP server shutdown.

## Shell Completions

Cobra generates completions for bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell automatically. See [assets/examples/completion.go](assets/examples/completion.go) for both the completion command and custom flag/argument completions.

## Testing CLI Commands

Test commands by executing them programmatically and capturing output. See [assets/examples/cli_test.go](assets/examples/cli_test.go).

Use `cmd.OutOrStdout()` and `cmd.ErrOrStderr()` in commands (instead of `os.Stdout` / `os.Stderr`) so output can be captured in tests.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Writing to `os.Stdout` directly | Tests can't capture output. Use `cmd.OutOrStdout()` which tests can redirect to a buffer |
| Calling `os.Exit()` inside `RunE` | Cobra's error handling, deferred functions, and cleanup code never run. Return an error, let `main()` decide |
| Not binding flags to Viper | Flags won't be configurable via env/config. Call `viper.BindPFlag` for every configurable flag |
| Missing `viper.SetEnvPrefix` | `PORT` collides with other tools. Use a prefix (`MYAPP_PORT`) to namespace env vars |
| Logging to stdout | Unix pipes chain stdout — logs corrupt the data stream for the next program. Logs go to stderr |
| Printing usage on every error | Full help text on every error is noise. Set `SilenceUsage: true`, save full usage for `--help` |
| Config file required | Users without a config file get a crash. Ignore `viper.ConfigFileNotFoundError` — config should be optional |
| Not using `PersistentPreRunE` | Config initialization must happen before any subcommand. Use root's `PersistentPreRunE` |
| Hardcoded version string | Version gets out of sync with tags. Inject via `ldflags` at build time from git tags |
| Not supporting `--output` format | Scripts can't parse human-readable output. Add JSON/table/plain for machine consumption |

## Related Skills

See `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-project-layout`, `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-dependency-injection`, `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-testing`, `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-design-patterns` skills.

package main

import (
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli/internal/deploy"
	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

type statusFlags struct {
	domain       string
	system       string
	gitopsRepo   string
	argocdServer string
	output       string
}

var statusFlagValues = statusFlags{output: deploy.OutputPlain}

var deployStatusCmd = &cobra.Command{
	Use:   "status <component>",
	Short: "Show what every environment runs, side by side",
	Long: "Report the release, image digest, age, sync state and health of a component in every environment " +
		"it is onboarded to, one row each.\n\n" +
		"This is the confirmation at the end of the release process. Promotion copies digests rather than " +
		"rebuilding, so the same digest in every row is what makes \"production runs the bits staging tested\" a " +
		"fact rather than a hope. The line under the table says whether that holds, and names the environments " +
		"that disagree when it does not.\n\n" +
		"The release, digest and age columns are read from the environment's overlay in the GitOps repository, " +
		"and dated by the commit that last changed it. Sync and health come from ArgoCD. An environment whose " +
		"overlay cannot be read, or that pins a tag rather than a digest, is reported rather than treated as an " +
		"error — the point of the table is the environments that are fine next to the one that is not. If ArgoCD " +
		"cannot be reached those two columns are left empty and everything else still prints.\n\n" +
		"Rows are ordered by the promotion graph in deploy.yaml, so the last row is the furthest downstream.\n\n" +
		"Nothing is written to git, no sync is triggered, and kubectl is never invoked. The exit code is 0 even " +
		"when the environments disagree; read `consistent` from --output json to gate on it.",
	Args:              cobra.ExactArgs(1),
	ValidArgsFunction: completeDeployComponents,
	RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
		if err := validateOutputFlag(statusFlagValues.output, deploy.OutputPlain, deploy.OutputJSON); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(cmd.Context(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
		defer cancel()

		return deploy.Status(ctx, deploy.StatusOptions{
			Component:    args[0],
			Domain:       statusFlagValues.domain,
			System:       statusFlagValues.system,
			GitopsRepo:   statusFlagValues.gitopsRepo,
			ArgocdServer: statusFlagValues.argocdServer,
			OutputFormat: statusFlagValues.output,
			UserAgent:    "intropy-cli/" + version,
			Stdout:       cmd.OutOrStdout(),
			Stderr:       cmd.ErrOrStderr(),
		})
	},
}

func init() {
	f := deployStatusCmd.Flags()
	f.StringVar(&statusFlagValues.domain, "domain", "", "disambiguate the component by domain")
	f.StringVar(&statusFlagValues.system, "system", "", "disambiguate the component by system")
	f.StringVar(&statusFlagValues.gitopsRepo, "gitops-repo", "", "GitOps repository URL (default: gitopsRepo from config, or INTROPY_GITOPS_REPO)")
	f.StringVar(&statusFlagValues.argocdServer, "argocd-server", "", "ArgoCD server to read from (default: argocdServer from config, ARGOCD_SERVER, or deploy.yaml)")
	f.StringVarP(&statusFlagValues.output, "output", "o", deploy.OutputPlain, "output format (plain, json)")

	// Deliberately no --env: status is every environment at once, and the
	// question about one of them — what a sync would apply — is deploy diff.
	_ = deployStatusCmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc("output", func(*cobra.Command, []string, string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
		return []string{deploy.OutputPlain, deploy.OutputJSON}, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
	})

	deployCmd.AddCommand(deployStatusCmd)
}

Without a version the commit comes from HEAD in the current source repository, which must be clean and pushed — CI builds pushed commits, so an unpushed one has no image — and the digests come from the tags CI published for it.

With a version the digests come from that release's manifest instead. The release already recorded them, so no source repository is read and the command works from any directory. ## Onboarding a system (`intropy deploy init`)

Every command below assumes the component already exists in the GitOps
repository. Getting it there used to be manual — hand-writing
`component.yaml`, `base/` and an overlay per environment, for every block, in
every customer repository. `deploy init` generates that tree from the topology
the system host declares:

```sh
# from a system workspace; --domain places the system in the tree
intropy deploy init --domain sales --plan
```

Everything the CLI can derive is filled in: each block's workload (an extractor
is a `CronJob`, everything else a `Deployment`), the app-ids that belong in a
Dapr component's `scopes:`, the environments `deploy.yaml` defines, the
registry. What it cannot derive — connection strings, hosts, credentials, cron
schedules — is emitted as a `REPLACE-ME-<HINT>` placeholder and listed when the
run finishes. Filling those in is the remaining job.

Image tags are never in that list. Scaffolding leaves them at an `unpinned`
sentinel, because pinning digests is `intropy deploy`'s job and nothing else's.

The system's shared objects — the Dapr pub/sub and secret store its blocks
resolve by name, plus the secrets behind them — go in a `host` directory of
their own, declared `kind: shared` in `component.yaml`:

```
domains/sales/ordersync/
  host/                    kind: shared — no image, nothing to pin
    base/dapr/pubsub.yaml  one owner, scopes: limits who may use it
    base/secrets/
  order-extract/           extractor ⇒ CronJob
  order-load/              loader ⇒ Deployment
```

A Dapr `Component` is namespace-scoped and every integration in the namespace
shares it, so exactly one ArgoCD Application may own each one. The `host`
directory is what gives them that owner; `scopes:` is what limits who may use
them. `deploy` and `promote` refuse a `kind: shared` component, since it has no
image to pin.

Which Dapr components get rendered depends on the platform, declared once per
repository in `deploy.yaml`:

```yaml
platform:
  provider: beebyte      # azure, beebyte, …
  pubsub: rabbitmq       # in-memory, rabbitmq, servicebus, …
  secretStore: kubernetes
```

The CLI itself knows nothing about any of those values: the string flows from
`deploy.yaml` into a template parameter and into a `spec.files` condition in the
template library, so adding a platform is a templates-repo change. The
components live in `base/` and are identical in every environment — what varies
per environment is the credential, which a Dapr component reaches through
`secretKeyRef`.

Nothing is pushed to the default branch; a tree full of placeholders would be
picked up by the ApplicationSet immediately. The run pushes
`deploy-init/<domain>-<system>` for review. Re-running is additive: a file that
already exists and differs is reported and left alone unless `--force` is given,
and `--force` still refuses to overwrite an overlay that pins a digest.

The topology comes from the host's `graph` verb, which builds the project first.
In CI, capture it once and skip the build:

```sh
dotnet run --project ./OrderSync.SystemHost -- graph > topology.json
intropy deploy init --domain sales --topology topology.json
```

environment's kustomize overlay in the GitOps repository.

=== CLAUDE.md ===
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code when working in this repository.

## What this repo is

A library of **Intropy templates**. Each template is a scaffold
rendered into a working project by the `intropy` CLI (separate repo:
`integrio-intropy/intropy-cli`). The CLI is the only renderer; this repo
contains content, not code.

The model is intentionally narrow: one engine (Go `text/template` + sprig),
one manifest format, one source of truth per template.

## Repository layout

```
<template>/
  template.yaml          # required: the intropy.dev/v1 manifest
  skeleton/              # required: rendered into the user's --output
    <files…>             # `.tmpl` files are templated; everything else is copied
  README.md              # optional: author-facing — what this template produces
  examples/              # optional: test fixtures for local renders
    minimal.yaml
    full.yaml
```

Rules:

- The CLI selects a template via positional argument:
  `intropy int create hello-world -o ./out`.
- Only `<template>/template.yaml` is parsed; only `<template>/skeleton/` is
  walked by the renderer.
- Anything else at the template root (README, examples, CHANGELOG, ADRs) is
  invisible to the renderer — it's for the template author, not the
  scaffolded project.
- There is **no shared content between templates**. No repo-level
  `skeletons/` dir, no cross-template includes. If two templates need the
  same file, duplicate it. (Composition happens at the *output* level:
  a template may declare whole sibling templates under `spec.dependencies`
  — see below — but never share skeleton files with them.)

## Manifest schema (`<template>/template.yaml`)

```yaml
apiVersion: intropy.dev/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: <kebab-case>           # convention: match the directory name
  title: <Title Case>
  description: <one sentence>
  tags: [example, go, http]
  labels:                      # two intropy.dev/* keys are load-bearing (see below)
    intropy.io/template-level: example
    intropy.dev/block-kind: extractor   # extractor | loader | aggregator | transactional-integration
    intropy.dev/data-flow: "in"         # in | out | both | internal
spec:
  parameters:                  # raw JSON Schema; type must be "object"
    type: object
    required: [name]
    properties:
      name:
        type: string
        title: Service name
        description: Lowercase kebab-case identifier.
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      port:
        type: integer
        default: 8080
  values:                      # optional; derived values rendered via Go template + sprig
    module: 'github.com/example/{{ .name }}'
  dependencies:                # optional; sibling templates scaffolded when missing
    - template: shared-contracts  # directory name in this repo
      output: '{{ .contracts }}'  # Go template; single path segment (conventionally "Contracts")
      values:                  # Go templates over this template's resolved values
        name: '{{ .contracts }}'
```

Notes:
